statement.p: Let p be the joint density function such that p(x,y) = \frac{1}{16} xy in R, the rectangle 0 \le x \le 4, 0\le y \le 2, and p(x,y)=0 outside R. Find the fraction of the population satisfying the constraint x \ge y

static.solution: p(x,y)=0 for all (x,y) outside the rectangle R, the population is given by the volume under the graph of p over the region inside the rectangle R and to the right of the line x=y. Therefore the fraction of the population is given by the double integral: \int_0^{2}\int_{y}^{4} \frac{1}{16} xy \,dx\, dy = \frac{1}{16} \int_0^{2} \frac{x^2y}{2} \bigg|_{y}^{4} dy = \frac{1}{16} \int_0^{2} \left(8 y - \frac{y^3}{2}\right) dy = \frac{1}{16} \left(4 y^2 - \frac {y^4}{8}\right)\bigg|_0^{2} = \frac{7}{8}
